focus: deepseek-01: The two-backend gate as code: what "Deem is available" means

label: /health is a pure dict read (status/model/backend) on the loopback route with no model pass; /v1/models is a redundant second source
A stub-backed server (no checkpoint) returns status ok; only the backend field (name=stub) refuses it, as deem-ctl already does
Model id defaults to deem-1.5 and is reported verbatim; the served id is deem-0.8-v1, so the pass condition needs a model-id pin
No authentication anywhere; Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* on every JSON answer and preflight, so any local process or open page can answer the probe
Failure statuses: 400 validation, 413 body_too_large, 400 unsupported_option_count, 404/405 routing, 500 backend_error/internal_error; shared error body shape
Weights load before the port binds, so a loading or absent server both read as connection refused; a port collision raises OSError in make_server
The MCP server is stdio JSON-RPC with no HTTP health surface and its own env-driven core/stub fallback; a different availability contract
Probe costs zero model passes; first real cost is one forward pass at /v1/systemone (LOCAL p50 60.2-60.5 ms warm); hook spawn cost stays unmeasured
Probe deadlines from installed settings: PreCompact 3 s, UserPromptSubmit 3 s each; probe budget must reserve the feature's own call
Both backends independent; preference per feature: Deem for payload-bearing/cheap/error-tolerant judgments, Jev for typed semantics or gold-calibrated decisions; per-feature switch only
No script or hook reads Deem /health today; the smallest missing harness is four stub-server fixtures (stub backend, wrong model, malformed, refused)
